newsitem.title: INDIA: India should implement panel report on gold -- trade.
newsitem.headline: India should implement panel report on gold -- trade.

text.p: The Indian government should implement without delay the views of an official committee on liberalising the country's gold policy, dealers and industry officials said on Tuesday.
"It is a radical step," said M.L. Damani, president of the Bombay Bullion Association referring to the panel's report. "The government must implement these recommendations with immediate effect."

A committee appointed by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Tuesday recommended that banks and financial institutions, fulfilling well defined criteria, should be permitted to operate freely both in domestic and international markets in gold.
It said sale of gold by banks and financial institutions should be allowed freely to all residents.
The committee also recommended that all banks may be allowed to offer gold-linked deposits and loans on the lines of foreign currency linked rupee deposits and loans for residents as suggested by it.
"I think it is a very positive move. It is about time banks are allowed to deal in gold," said Khursheeda Mody, head of the Geneva-based World Gold Council's India operations.

The panel said in its first phase banks fulfilling certain well-defined criteria may be allowed to mobilise household gold for providing working capital gold loans to jewellery manufacturers as also traders.
"Banks may also be encouraged to grant loans against gold denominated deposits," it said.
Damani said trade would immensely benefit by the proposal on gold loans to jewellery manufacturers.
"This will give an opportunity to the Indian consumers to use gold, not merely to convert it into jewellery, but as an investment product," Mody said.
She expected the first phase of the recommendations to be implemented between now and end of 1988.
"We hope that it happens as fast as possible," Mody said.
Damani said gold trade in Turkey, Italy and Malaysia was more or less free and the committee had been thinking in similar lines.
The panel in its report said it would be useful to study the gold financing schemes and measures to foster markets in Italy, Turkey and Malaysia.
The committee said in the second phase government and RBI should take steps to develop a well regulated market in India for gold and gold derivatives, including forward trading.
Both residents and non-residents should be allowed to operate in this market, subject to adherence to certain well defined guidelines, it said.
